title: Sort Zeros, Ones and Twos

concept.title: Three regions with three pointers
body: An array that holds only 0, 1 and 2 can be sorted in **one pass without extra memory**. Keep three regions: zeros at the front (before `lo`), twos at the back (after `hi`), and the unknown part between `mid` and `hi`. Look at `a[mid]`:
After swapping with `hi` do not move `mid`: the element that came from the back has not been looked at yet. This is the "Dutch national flag" algorithm.

statement: You are given an array that contains only the numbers 0, 1 and 2. Sort it in increasing order and print it.
inputFormat: The second line has `n` numbers, each 0, 1 or 2.
outputFormat: Print the sorted array on one line.
hints: Keep three regions: zeros, ones and twos, and an unknown region in the middle.
A 0 is swapped to the front region, a 2 is swapped to the back region, a 1 stays.
After swapping a 2 to the back, do not advance `mid` yet.

explanation: Zeros are swapped to the front and twos to the back while `mid` scans. When the scan meets the twos region, everything is in place.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

lo = mid = 0
hi = n - 1
while mid <= hi:
    if a[mid] == 0:
        a[lo], a[mid] = a[mid], a[lo]
        lo += 1
        mid += 1
    elif a[mid] == 1:
        mid += 1
    else:
        a[mid], a[hi] = a[hi], a[mid]
        hi -= 1
print(*a)
